claims.claim_text: The Republican Party calls on the U.S. government to improve protection of federal systems containing sensitive data and controlling important U.S. facilities.
The Republican Party calls for immediately updating the U.S. government-information-system security law drafted roughly a decade before its 2012 platform.

The Republican Party assesses U.S. government-industry cyberthreat information sharing and free information flow within the private sector as the most effective means of combating potential cybersecurity threats.

The Republican Party characterizes the laws and policies of the U.S. administration in office in 2012 as undermining government-private-sector collaboration and disadvantaging both sectors in proactively identifying potential cyberthreats.
The Republican Party predicts that the regulatory approach of the U.S. administration in office in 2012 will increase federal bureaucracy's size and cost and harm cybersecurity innovation.
The U.S. government collects valuable information about potential cyberthreats that can be shared with private entities without compromising national security.
The Republican Party calls for the U.S. government to share valuable potential-cyberthreat information with private entities without compromising national security.
The Republican Party calls for removing legal and regulatory barriers preventing or deterring companies from voluntarily sharing cyberthreat information with their U.S. government partners.
